sources.review: Kashika applies at augmentation and p-it status to first-person Lot. Nyasa assigns p-it to the ending, not the augment, and explicitly connects absence of ng-it to guna. Both padas are illustrated.
A non-p-it sarvadhatuka is treated as ng-it. Nyasa explicitly warns that Lot p-it applies to the ending, not the intervening augment or class suffix.
k/ng-conditioned guna/vrddhi prohibition is contextual; a rule ID anywhere in a trace does not identify which suffix conditions the root.
Deletion of a in sna(m) and as requires a following k/ng-it sarvadhatuka; non-k/ng examples preserve a.
Long i replaces sna/reduplicated a before consonant-initial k/ng-it sarvadhatuka, excluding ghu roots. Balamanorama directly contrasts mimi-vah/mah forms with Lot mima-vahai/mahai forms.
Deletion of non-cluster-preceded suffix u before m/v is optional; both retained-u and deleted-u weak forms must remain accepted.
Jahati has optional short-i alongside long-i before consonant-initial k/ng-it sarvadhatuka; both appear in the ha control.
Stumbh/skumbh license both sna and snu. Sautra does not restrict these entries to this one formation. Mixed branch coverage is valid but prevents an every-answer 6.4.113 interpretation.
Guna of a final ik before a sarvadhatuka/ardhadhatuka, subject to blocking conditions, explains the strengthened nu/u suffix.
Light penultimate ik guna subject to the conditioning suffix explains lih→leh; root-vowel and class-suffix strengthening must be distinguished.
Root markers restrict Atmanepada; Kartari is not synonymous with Parasmaipada.
Svarita/ny-it roots take Atmanepada under agent-benefiting-result interpretation. With no such context specified, the task accepts any licensed form rather than choosing one hidden pada.
Parasmaipada applies to the remaining Kartari contexts. Unspecified pada means a licensed union, not unrestricted replacement of all roots by either ending.
Sas has a lexical and k/ng-it-conditioned i alternation; its singleton branch was excluded from this fixed panel, avoiding an unsupported general branch extrapolation.

The trnah im augment additionally requires consonant-initial p-it; the printed Lot first-person forms lack im. Thus p-it alone is not a universal rule that the entire word matches its present strong stem.
